example.en: Sara wants to get her driving licence.

example.nl: Ik heb twee keer per week rijles.
example.en: I have a driving lesson twice a week.

example.nl: De rijschool is dichtbij mijn huis.
example.en: The driving school is close to my house.

example.nl: Parkeren in Amsterdam is moeilijk en duur.
example.en: Parking in Amsterdam is difficult and expensive.
I can't find a parking space.

example.en: We still need to fill up.
Petrol is expensive in the Netherlands.

example.nl: Op de snelweg mag je honderd rijden.
example.en: On the motorway you can do a hundred.

grammar.title: tenzij (unless) and zolang (as long as)
points: tenzij means 'unless' and zolang means 'as long as' (or 'while').
Both start a subordinate clause, so the verb goes to the end: ..., tenzij er file is.
When the clause comes first, the main clause starts with the verb: Zolang je les hebt, rijdt de instructeur mee.
tenzij already means 'if not', so don't add an extra niet: We gaan, tenzij het regent (We'll go unless it rains).
zolang is about time or a condition that lasts: Zolang de motor koud is, moet je rustig rijden.

examples.nl: We gaan met de auto, tenzij er file is.
examples.en: We'll go by car, unless there's a traffic jam.

examples.nl: Zolang je les hebt, rijdt de instructeur met je mee.
examples.en: As long as you're taking lessons, the instructor drives with you.

examples.en: I don't drive on the motorway unless my instructor is sitting next to me.

examples.nl: Zolang de motor koud is, moet je rustig rijden.
examples.en: As long as the engine is cold, you should drive gently.

examples.nl: Je mag hier niet parkeren, tenzij je hier woont.

dialogue.title: Rijles op de snelweg
dialogue.scene: Sara is taking driving lessons. Today her instructor Kees wants to take her onto the motorway for the first time.

lines.speaker: Kees
lines.nl: Goed, Sara. Start de motor maar.
lines.en: Right, Sara. Go ahead and start the engine.

lines.speaker: Kees
lines.nl: Rustig. Je moet eerst je voet op de rem zetten.
lines.en: Relax. You have to put your foot on the brake first.

lines.speaker: Kees
lines.nl: Mooi. We gaan vandaag de snelweg op, tenzij je dat te eng vindt.
lines.en: Good. We're going onto the motorway today, unless you find that too scary.

lines.speaker: Sara
lines.nl: Een beetje eng, maar zolang u naast me zit, gaat het wel.
lines.en: A bit scary, but as long as you're sitting next to me, I'll be fine.

lines.speaker: Kees
lines.nl: Niet te snel. Op deze snelweg mag je honderd.
lines.en: Not too fast. On this motorway you can do a hundred.

lines.speaker: Kees
lines.nl: Ja, maar kijk eerst in je spiegel. Goed zo!
lines.en: Yes, but check your mirror first. Well done!

lines.speaker: Sara
lines.en: Look, there's a traffic jam there.

lines.speaker: Kees
lines.nl: Dan gaan we hier van de snelweg af. Daarna moeten we nog tanken.
lines.en: Then we'll get off the motorway here. After that we still need to fill up.

lines.speaker: Sara
lines.nl: En parkeren? Daar ben ik niet goed in.
lines.en: And parking? I'm not good at that.

lines.speaker: Kees
lines.nl: Dat oefenen we morgen. Zolang je oefent, word je beter.
lines.en: We'll practise that tomorrow. As long as you keep practising, you'll get better.
